title: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN
description: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN adds a new column to an existing table, without touching the rows already in it. Add a column named `loyalty_points` (INTEGER) to the `customers` table.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: ALTER TABLE, ADD COLUMN
ALTER TABLE names the table you're changing, and ADD COLUMN names the new column and its type - existing rows automatically get NULL in the new column unless you specify a DEFAULT.
Target the customers table, and give the new column the exact name loyalty_points with type INTEGER.
expected_behavior: customers gains a loyalty_points INTEGER column; existing rows get NULL in it.
solution: ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN loyalty_points INTEGER;
explanation: ALTER TABLE is how a schema evolves after a table already has data in it - CREATE TABLE only runs once, but ALTER TABLE is what you reach for from then on.

hidden_tests.check_query: SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'fixtures' AND table_name = 'customers' AND column_name = 'loyalty_points'
